judge_reasoning: The model misunderstands skulk, assuming large attackers are hard to block. In fact skulk only prevents blocks by creatures with strictly greater power, so a big Gideon (5/5 or 6/6, actually 6/6 with the emblem) can be blocked by any of the opponent's creatures. The opponent has a legal blocking assignment (Seraph blocks Gideon, Sparring Mummy blocks Temmet, Labyrinth Guardian blocks Knight #2) that leaves only the unblockable Knight #1 (4 power) getting through, dealing only 4 damage instead of the required 7, so the opponent survives at 3 life. The official solution instead exploits skulk correctly by shrinking Gideon and the Knight token to 1 power, making them unblockable by any of the opponent's higher-power creatures, then restoring Gideon's power after blocks are locked in. The model's plan fails against reasonable opponent blocking.
model_solution:
1. Cast Temmet, Vizier of Naktamun for {W}{U}
2. Activate Gideon's +1 ability (Gideon becomes 5/5 creature with indestructible)
3. Activate Gideon's 0 ability (create a second 2/2 Knight Ally token)
4. Enter combat
5. At beginning of combat, Temmet's ability triggers targeting Knight #1 (the original token), making it 4/4 and unblockable
6. Attack with all four creatures: Temmet (3/3), Gideon (5/5), Knight #1 (4/4 unblockable), Knight #2 (3/3)
7. Opponent can only block one creature with Labyrinth Guardian due to skulk restriction
8. Declare blockers - even if Guardian blocks Gideon, Knight #1 deals 4 unblocked damage, Temmet deals 3 unblocked, Knight #2 deals 3 unblocked = 10 total damage, exceeding opponent's 7 life total
